questions.q: Why did Meridian's zero trust rollout score well on its maturity audit despite the breach described in this case study?
options: The audit scored every pillar as Traditional, so the result was misleadingly low rather than high
The CISA model does not include a way to score Networks or Identity
The legacy SFTP export was formally excluded from the audit's scope, so the breach happened through something the audit was never measuring
The auditor was bribed to overlook the gap
questions.explain: A maturity audit checks what's in scope by design -- the excluded system simply wasn't part of what was being measured.

questions.q: Why was svc-claimflow-sftp never covered by the Conditional Access policy from Lesson 29?
options: Because that service account had already been deleted
Because Conditional Access cannot apply to any service account under any circumstances
Because ClaimFlow refused to allow Conditional Access on their systems
Because the policy applied to interactive sign-ins, and the SFTP job was a scheduled, non-interactive process
questions.explain: The gap was a scope mismatch: the policy covered interactive sign-ins, and this account never generated one.

questions.q: What made 'scope exclusion #4' dangerous in hindsight, even though it was a reasonable decision the day it was written?
options: It granted MFA bypass to every employee at Meridian
It was never reviewed by anyone at any point
Nothing automatically re-triggered a review when the decommission date it depended on slipped by four months
It excluded Identity and Networks from the entire audit
questions.explain: An exemption tied to a timeline needs an automatic re-check when that timeline slips -- otherwise it quietly becomes permanent.

questions.q: What is the main point this case study makes about audit scope versus security scope?
options: Maturity audits should be abandoned entirely in favor of informal reviews
What a checklist measures is not automatically the same as what actually needs protecting, and that gap is where this breach lived
Every system should always be included in every audit with no exceptions ever
Audits are only useful for cloud systems, never for on-prem or legacy ones
questions.explain: The scoring itself wasn't wrong -- the gap between what was measured and what needed protecting is the real lesson.

questions.q: Which fix would have limited the damage even while svc-claimflow-sftp stayed outside the main identity fabric?
options: Applying assume-breach containment -- scoping that account's read access down to only the claims folder it actually needed
Redesigning the entire micro-segmentation scheme from Lesson 29
Replacing Entra ID with a different identity provider
Removing the audit's scope-exclusion process entirely
questions.explain: Assume-breach design exists for exactly this case: a control everyone assumed would hold didn't, so blast-radius limits still had to apply.
